title: Nodes
description: The machines: CPU, load, memory, disk, network (node-exporter).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the last boot. A short uptime that you did not expect = the node rebooted or lost power.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: 5-minute load average divided by the number of cores. 1.0 = all cores busy.

panels.title: Clock synced
panels.description: 1 = the kernel clock is in sync (NTP). 0 = not in sync. TLS and etcd need a correct clock.

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Where the CPU time goes, for all selected nodes. High iowait = the CPU waits for the disk. High softirq = much network traffic.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: Load = processes that run or wait for a CPU, plus processes that wait for disk I/O. Divided by the cores: 1.0 = all cores busy. High load with low CPU used = the node waits for the disk. Solid line = 1 minute, dashed = 15 minutes.

panels.title: Processes running
panels.description: Processes that run or wait for a CPU now.

panels.title: CPU throttling
panels.description: The CPU slows down because it is too hot. On a Raspberry Pi, this means: check the cooling.

panels.title: OOM kills
panels.description: The kernel stopped a process because the memory was full. This also counts processes outside of Kubernetes.

panels.title: Major page faults
panels.description: Memory pages that the kernel must read from the disk. Many = too little memory for the page cache.

panels.title: Swap in and out (in up, out down)
panels.description: Pages per second. Constant swap traffic makes the node slow.

panels.title: Filesystem free
panels.description: Look at the slope: a line that goes down fast fills the disk soon.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Part of the time when the disk had at least one request. Near 100% = the disk is the bottleneck. mmcblk = SD card, nvme = NVMe SSD, sd = SATA, USB or iSCSI, dm = LVM volume.

panels.title: Disk latency (read up, write down)
panels.description: Average time for one request. SSD: below 1 ms. SD card and iSCSI: often 10 ms or more.

panels.title: Network errors and drops (rx up, tx down)
panels.description: Errors = bad packets (cable, NIC, driver). Drops = the kernel had no space for the packet.

panels.title: TCP retransmits
panels.description: Part of the sent TCP segments that were sent again. Above 1% = packet loss on the network.

panels.title: TCP connections
panels.description: Open TCP sockets and sockets in TIME_WAIT.

panels.title: conntrack table used
panels.description: Connection tracking for NAT and the firewall. When it is full, the kernel drops new connections.
